orrowen: Cadhan o hosen re yal cadhat lona
meanings: This we lay as it was laid for us (Halyna's close, in the dual: 'we two lay it as it was laid at us two')
derivation: a phrase: Cadhan lay-1DU (cadh + -An, broad) + o it(+S) + hosen as + re PST(+S) + yal S·be.PST + cadhat laid + lona at-1DU; the frame of O0238 (1sg) and O0234 (1pl) with the pair's own person, as orrowen_v2 §3.9 item 1 requires ('Where the Book gives Halyna a plural verb, the Orrowen original is dual'); unit S06 (IV.1)

derivation: a phrase: ul vodh where + naross absent (na- + S·doss) + poduloth wisdom (podul + -Oth) + hessyth restraint (hess 'stop', the Guest's first word, + -Oth) + ol our(+N) + lestir guide (l unchanged); verbless, as Grest um hos, grest um vana; unit S06 (IV.1)

meanings: Stone does not translate ('translating is not at stone': stone cannot carry words across); IV.1, after Veth lymm tolm nayalat, 'But stone carries nothing'
derivation: a phrase: nath NEG(+N) + noss N·doss + brodlymmyl translating (brodlymm 'word-carry' + -Ol) + lo at(+S) + dholm S·tolm; the 'at' idiom of ability (orrowen_v2 §3.7), as Seren's Nath noss tul kethyl … lo Halyna. Said this way because nath + brodlymm would bed to mrodlymm, an onset §2.5 does not allow; unit S06 (IV.1)

meanings: Corporal Voss (the title before the name, as Crennel Kael 'Sergeant Kael'); Voss who asked
derivation: a phrase: kesterd a corporal (kest 'a company' + -Ard) + Voss (a name; names are names); unit S06 (IV.5)

meanings: in one's cups, over the ale ('at the cups'); lo so nunthath, in their cups
derivation: a phrase: lo at(+S) + nunthath cups (nunth + -Ath; n unchanged); unit S06 (IV.5: Re rytent lo so nunthath, 'They swore in their cups')

meanings: the floating stones (of Highreach, Taldow Helv: 'the stones that float'); et tolmath sa haemerent; the Book's 'the tower of the floating stones' is taldow et tolmath sa haemerent (unit S05). NB haemer is also 'hang': Re haemerent et tolmath (IV.1 ¶11) is 'the stones hung'; this phrase is the stones that float
derivation: a phrase: tolmath stones (tolm + -Ath) + sa REL(+S; h unchanged) + haemerent float-3PL (haemer 'a raft; to float; hang, float' + -Ant; the relative verb agrees with the plural it stands for, S06 S8); unit S06 (IV.1 ¶4: into the cranes of Highreach that lifted the floating stones), and S05 (Taldow Helv, taldow et tolmath sa haemerent). Added by the S06 back-translation: without the row a reader takes haemer as 'hang', as the leaf itself uses it three times
